version.changelog: 补 ClawHub 分类标签（operations）与话题

llm.summary: This is a real OSS static-site deployment skill, but it needs Review because it can reuse local GitHub credentials and make cloud storage publicly accessible.

dimensions.detail: The cloud and repository authority is purpose-related, but it includes disabling OSS BlockPublicAccess, public-read hosting, DNS/CAS changes, GitHub repository secret mutation, and directory uploads without strong dedicated-bucket or confirmation safeguards.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal git clone or manual skill-folder copy with PyPI dependencies; I found no post-install hook or remote script execution, though installing the skill makes broad deployment triggers available to the agent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad trigger phrases and instructs agents to parse ~/.git-credentials and configure Git to use the plaintext store helper; those are high-impact credential behaviors that are not sufficiently gated by explicit user consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent local backups, ACME state, and unencrypted certificate private keys, suggests scheduled renewal, and can modify repository Git credential-helper configuration; these are expected for deployment automation but under-scoped for safe defaults.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package is broadly coherent with its stated purpose: scripts cover public static build cleanup, OSS upload, website hosting, certificate issuance/distribution, GitHub Actions secrets/variables, and deployment verification.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent changing OSS bucket public-access settings, DNS/certificate configuration, and GitHub Actions secrets. Use a dedicated public-only bucket, a least-privilege Alibaba RAM user, and an explicitly provided least-privilege GitHub token instead of allowing fallback to ~/.git-credentials. Store certificate material in a private directory with restrictive permissions and review the upload directory before making it public.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: individual helper scripts do not each implement the whole advertised workflow, but together the artifact contains build, deploy, certificate, GitHub secret, and verification components matching the skill purpose.
[PE3] unexpected: Confirmed concern: SKILL.md and set_github_secret.py read ~/.git-credentials as a fallback GitHub token source, which silently expands authority beyond an explicitly supplied task token.
[SDI-2] expected: Confirmed concern in context: public OSS hosting requires public access, but deploy_oss.py can disable bucket-level public-access blocking and verify anonymous access without strong protection against reusing a bucket containing unintended objects.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly confirmed: the skill discusses public access and includes a build cleanup script, but warnings and guardrails are not strong enough for a workflow that can expose bucket contents to the internet.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded for build_static.py: references to .env, .npmrc, and .netrc are deny-list exclusions to keep secrets out of public artifacts, not credential harvesting.
[SC2] expected: Downgraded: the curl examples contact expected OSS/GitHub endpoints for checks or API calls; I did not find remote code download-and-execute behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed coding risk: cert_manager.py creates ~/.acme-oss certificate material and writes unencrypted private keys without explicit restrictive file modes, leaving permissions to the process umask.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly confirmed: manifest and README triggers such as generic deployment or上线 phrases are broader than ideal for a skill that can change cloud, DNS, certificate, and GitHub repository state.
